fresh_observations.status: New bounded consumer elaboration of an existing historical negative-radius contract; supported ingress and unique alias/count unresolved.
fresh_observations.analysis: MeshCollider.new publicly stores raw reach. Closest traversal squares max_distance, but the hair collider returns the unsquared reach and synthetic up on a miss. For an otherwise valid closed mesh near the origin, a point far above it, reach -1 m and offset 0, the point remains outside the 1 m search radius while push_out can execute all six roughly 1 m upward corrections. This follows source control flow and real-number/ordinary finite-f32 reasoning; no geometry fixture, product code or runtime has been executed.
fresh_observations.safeguards_and_limits: The ordinary creator paths shown pass positive BODY_REACH=0.1 m; no supported caller accepting negative reach was established. A positive bounded search miss and intentional NoCollider infinity are distinct states. The trait admits custom query implementations, and actual GPU/native numeric behavior is unobserved.

fresh_observations.future_direction: Decide supported reach/sign and no-hit contracts at the owning boundary and trace actual producers; preserve intentional unlimited or no-obstacle states. No repair or validation has begun.

fresh_observations.status: Fresh independent corroboration and consumer ordering refinement of the earlier 95e hair-field assessment and historical F054 topology admission; no duplicate count asserted.
fresh_observations.analysis: BodySurface exposes public position and face slices. GroomedHair.place first calls BodyField.sample; its NearMesh.upload copies positions and calls vertex_normals on raw faces before GPU uploads and before the later CPU MeshCollider.new. vertex_normals indexes positions before any visible local index-membership check. If prior field setup reaches that call with an empty positions list and a face containing index 0, that index is the first demonstrated operation on that route; no actual malformed body or runtime failure was demonstrated. The later MeshCollider constructor separately calls the same normals helper before TriangleBvh.new. On-bust construction uses a generated head mesh and is a distinct route.
fresh_observations.safeguards_and_limits: Some preceding field setup and external GPU objects must be available before NearMesh.upload; inspect upstream body producers and successful body-field admission rather than assuming they permit malformed inputs. No actual vertex/face validation policy or device behavior is inferred from this window.

fresh_observations.status: Independent fresh corroboration and reconciliation of prior checkpoint19 no-hit question; no additional count.
fresh_observations.analysis: With positive reach, an interior point farther than reach from every triangle can return a positive synthetic outside distance, because the closest query finds no triangle inside its radius. A closed cube whose center is 0.2 m from each face, queried at the center with reach 0.1 m, is a geometric counterexample; no model or fixture is built. ScalpCap.fit treats a miss as a real distance and normal, so before clear_skin a returned (0.1,up) shifts a carried point down by approximately 0.0996 m. Later sampled correction might change it; no final geometry or actual ordinary-body miss is established.
fresh_observations.safeguards_and_limits: The documented implementation intentionally reports a miss as far outside; a producer guarantee that all projection points are within 0.1 m could make the intended route safe. Clear-skin passes inspect only selected samples. Creator GPU strand LOD uses a separate field buffer, while cap fitting receives the CPU MeshCollider.
fresh_observations.relationship: The checkpoint19 prior report already raised the same conditional no-hit and cap projection question. Original 059 Lens13 read cap.rs but explicitly left MeshCollider query proof pending; other original collider reviewers excluded lines112–164. Distinct from the mixed-infinite shrinkwrap observation; alias remains central.
fresh_observations.future_direction: Establish supported point/reach placement contract and miss handling through projection without changing legitimate no-obstacle semantics; compare implementations only after separate authorization.

fresh_observations.status: Fresh corroboration of prior checkpoint19 and 059 open sampled-versus-continuous question; no additional count.
fresh_observations.analysis: For a straight 0.08 m first segment on x, an exact sphere signed-distance function centered at x=0.01 m with radius 0.004 m and clearance 0.0015 m yields an intersecting interval 0.006–0.014 m. Its first endpoint signed distance 0.006 m makes the early endpoint/reach skip inapplicable, but quarter, half and three-quarter sample distances 0.006, 0.026 and 0.046 m all exceed clearance; the loop can exit without moving the crossing. This is mathematical reasoning about a trait-permitted sphere, not an instantiated fixture or evidence of a shipped generated hairstyle.
fresh_observations.safeguards_and_limits: Fewer than two points return, the root is intentionally fixed, and passes are bounded. Four-pass cards and host LOD callers are shown, but neither establishes which concrete collider reaches them or that continuous clearance is required; the scalp-cap triangle sampler is a different function.
fresh_observations.relationship: 059 READ-L11-432 already recorded that three samples do not establish continuous segment clearance. The checkpoint19 report has the same counterexample; original Lens13 cap sampling is related but not presumed identical.
fresh_observations.future_direction: Decide continuous-clearance versus sampled approximation policy, allowable error and fixed-root behavior; preserve intended finite work bounds.

fresh_observations.analysis: Shrinkwrap computes a displacement even when a locked or clear point gets zero weight; if another point makes any true, a mixed finite/infinite query result can propagate nonfinite motion. If NoCollider alone supplies infinity for every point, every weight is zero and the early return prevents applying the computed moves. No mixed-distance producer was established.

nonfindings: NoCollider reports positive infinity with up as an intentional no-obstacle sentinel; all-NoCollider shrinkwrap exits before applying its computed moves.
Assigned MeshCollider stores its copied positions, normals, triangles and BVH in private fields; no stale mutation of that private state was shown.
A positive finite reach fallback may be intentional for bounded near-surface inputs; no universally valid projection condition or actual miss was proved.
The current physics MeshCollider records are not automatically about the unrelated fabelgeist-hair MeshCollider despite the name.
open_questions: Which public or decoded paths can construct negative, zero, nonfinite or extreme positive reach, and what policy should each query and consumer use?
Do supported creator placements guarantee every scalp cap point and every required query is within 0.1 m of a valid closed body surface?

Which BodySurface producers establish vertex/face membership, finite geometry, winding, nondegeneracy and normals before NearMesh upload or CPU construction, and what invalid/empty behavior is intended?
Which host cards/LOD paths actually receive which Collider, and do their callers require continuous clearance, bounded-error sampling or a different result?
Can a supported Collider return a mixture of finite and infinite distances? What actual rendering, native GPU and full geometry consequences would follow? None were executed or validated.
Exact repair owner, relationship to F054/CONTRACT-628/current head index/field capacity, unique count and all broader historical/other-lens obligations remain centrally unresolved.
